pages.text: 1. Purpose and Application: Purpose Application Comments (Plant Specific) To define a standard work instruction for manually swabbing a forming machine. This work instruction applies to all O-I manufacturing facilities. Plants may enter text and images in the [ ] areas in this column. Place large images, tables etc. in the Appendix. 1. Safety Safety Requirements Observe O-I standard safety requirements and procedures defined by the Global Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S) organization, as well as all applicable local, regional, and national requirements. Safety equipment and instructions specific to the completion of this work instruction are detailed in the Instructions Section. Danger Slip Crush Hand Hot Surface Bump Hazard Warning Inhalation Steam 1. Instructions: 1. Before starting the work instruction activity, perform the following steps:

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Do not begin these tasks without confirmation that personnel directly involved have completed the required training associated with the work instruction activity and have reviewed this document. Plants may enter specifications and requirements from the MSDR for anything other than the information already defined in the product quality specifications / control plans 1. Gather necessary tools and equipment as identified below in the Equipment Section. 1. Wear and use additional PPE and safety equipment required for this specific work instruction. Plant Leader: refer to MSDR to insert global requirements, then add any additional plant requirements. NOTE: the plant requirements can be stricter, never looser than global requirements 1. Obey all applicable safety requirements and procedures. 1. To prepare the swab brushes, perform the following steps: Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Begin each shift with new, clean swab brushes of the appropriate diameter and length per the job history. Replace them during the shift as needed. 1. Use one swab brush for the neckrings. 1. Use two swab brushes for the blanks, swabbing half of the sections with each brush.

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Prepare a new swab brush by saturating it with a light oil so that the swab lubricant compound will penetrate into the swab fibers. 1. Inspect the swab brushes before each swab cycle. Replace a swab brush if it becomes hard or scorched, is losing fibers, forms a tail, or is no longer soft, fluffy and able to apply the proper coat of swabbing compound. Bad Swab Brush 1. When a swab is no longer useable, remove the head and place it into a designated container per regional or country specific environmental regulations. 1. Only use the approved commercial swabbing compound specified in the swabbing instructions. Do not add other materials to the approved compounds, or mix commercial compounds to create alternate swabbing compounds. 1. Properly maintain swabs and swab stations to reduce or eliminate the chance of contamination of swabs or swab compound. 1. Clean swab pots (dope buckets) when contaminated, with a minimum cleaning of once per day or as specified by plant procedures. 1. To properly swab a section, perform the following steps:

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Review the established swabbing instructions for the job being produced. 1. Determine the minimum number of cycles to reject ware after swabbing based on the control document or a checklist. 1. Perform swabbing at the prescribed frequency established for the job being produced, and in a consistent manner for each swabbing cycle. 1. Do not make any changes to the prescribed swabbing cycles or materials defined by the job history unless changes are approved by the appropriate supervisor. 1. Before swabbing a section, activate the “Swab Cycle” switch on the section control panel. NOTE: it is recommended that the “Swab Cycle” be activated when the baffle is down. 1. The Manual swab light will begin to blink, gob loading will stop, and the section will clear glass from the blank side. 2. If equipped, the blank side safety barrier will go down. 3. The blanks will remain open, and the invert will stay on the blank side. 4. Do not use the swab cycle switch to change blank side equipment. Swab Cycle Switch 1. Begin swabbing when the “RUN” indicator light starts blinking, the blank side is clear of glass, and the neckring arms are in the revert position. Run Indicator Light

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. When swabbing, hold the swab along the metal handle with an overhand grip. NOTE: If your plant uses swabs with a ring on the end, do not put your thumb through the ring. Serious injuries to your thumb or fingers may result if the swab gets caught in the section. Do not place thumb or fingers in the ring! 1. Stand comfortably and balanced, and keep your free hand away from moving parts while swabbing. 1. It is recommended that swabbing occur from the inside cavity to the outside cavity, working toward yourself. 1. If a swab gets caught in equipment, let go immediately and push the E-STOP button for the section. 1. For each swab cycle, change the starting section to prevent the build-up of lubrication and provide more uniform lubrication to each section. 1. For example, when swabbing sections 1-5 of a 10-section machine, the first swab cycle would

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) start on section #1 (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), the next swab cycle would start with section #2 (2, 3, 4, 5, 1), etc. 2. When swabbing sections 6-10, the first swab cycle would start on section #6 (6, 7, 8, 9, 10), the next swab cycle would start with section #7 (7, 8, 9, 10, 6), etc. 1. After swabbing a section and your hand is clear of the section, deactivate the swab cycle by cycling the button. 1. The RUN light continues to blink until normal operations resume, then stays on continuously. 2. If equipped, the blank side safety barrier will go up. 3. Glass will start loading again. 4. Ware will be rejected for a defined number of cycles after the swabbing event. 1. Examine ware before and after swabbing for several cycles to determine if any adverse effects resulted from swabbing with the exception of ABL system. 1. To swab the neckrings, perform the following steps: Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) NOTE: It is recommended that neckrings be swabbed before swabbing the blanks.

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Prepare swab brushes according to the job history. 1. Apply a small amount of neckring swab compound on the swab and work it into the fibers of the swab. 2. Wring out excess lubricant with a twisting motion, and shake the swab so that it loosens back out. 1. Bend the head of the swab at a 45-90 degree angle to prevent damage to the neckring from the metal tip. 1. Do not bend the swab if the swab has a protective tip (such as those used in the Asia- Pacific region). 1. Use the swab-cycle switch to swab the neckrings, as explained in Section 3.3. NOTE: It is recommended that you activate the “Swab Cycle” when the baffle is down. Swab Cycle Switch 1. Do not put your thumb or finger through the ring on the swab brush handle, if your plant uses swabs with a ring. NOTE: Serious injuries to your thumb or fingers may result if the swab gets caught in the section. Do not place thumb or fingers in the ring!

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. It is recommended that swabbing occur from the inside cavity to the outside cavity, working toward yourself. 1. Swab each neckring once with a downward dabbing or patting motion. 1. A proper swab will leave an imprint of the neckring on the swab. 2. Do not use a sliding or back-and-forth motion, or drag the swab across the rings, because this will leave excess lubricant on the neckring. 1. Swab half of the machine section neckrings, then reapply the neckring swab compound and swab the remaining sections. 1. For each swab cycle, change the starting section to prevent the build-up of lubrication and provide more uniform lubrication to each section. 1. For example, when swabbing sections 1-5 of a 10-section machine, the first swab cycle would start on section #1 (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), the next swab cycle would start with section #2 (2, 3, 4, 5, 1), etc. 2. When swabbing sections 6-10, the first swab cycle would start on section #6 (6, 7, 8, 9, 10), the next swab cycle would start with section #7 (7, 8, 9, 10, 6), etc. 1. To swab the blanks, perform the following steps:

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) NOTE: It is recommended that neckrings be swabbed before swabbing the blanks. 1. Swab all blanks according to established swabbing instructions. 1. When uncoated blanks are changed, increase the swabbing frequency to every 10 minutes for an hour in order to build up a coating/layer on the inside of the equipment. 2. Pre-coated blanks do not require extra swabbing. Pre-Coated Uncoated

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Use the proper size swab for the blank cavity. 1. The swab should not be more than 1.5 times the diameter of the blank at the load line. 2. If the swab is too big, it will apply a coat of lubricant on the face of the blank that will create defects such as heavy seams. 3. If the swab is too small, it will not cover the entire blank cavity. 4. If needed, cut the swab fibers to the correct size. 5. Do not burn a swab down to size because that produces rough ends that scrub off the lubricant. 1. Prepare swab brushes according to the job history. 1. Apply a small amount of blank swab compound to the swab and work it into the fibers. 2. Squeeze out excess swab compound, and shake the swab to loosen the fibers. 3. Do not allow swab compound to run or drip down the blanks because this can cause carbon buildup, affect gob loading, and cause a jam-up.

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) Shaken Not Shaken 1. Use the swab-cycle switch to swab the neckrings, as explained in Section 3.3. NOTE: It is recommended that you activate the “Swab Cycle” when the baffle is down. 1. Do not put your thumb or finger through the ring on the swab brush handle, if your plant uses swabs with a ring. NOTE: Serious injuries to your thumb or fingers may result if the swab gets caught in the section. Do not place thumb or fingers in the ring!

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Always apply light pressure to the blanks, and hold the swab parallel to the blank. This technique will apply lubricant only to the blank cavity and keep the face of the blank clean. 1. If possible, rotate the swab brush after swabbing each blank (both sides) and shake it slightly. This will ensure that a uniform amount of lubricant is applied to each blank, and will maintain even wear and increase the life of the swab. 1. It is recommended that swabbing occur from the inside cavity to the outside cavity, working toward yourself. 1. Swab half of the machine sections with one brush, then swab the remaining sections with the other brush. For larger machines, reduce the number of sections swabbed with a single brush. 1. For each swab cycle, change the starting section to prevent the build-up of lubrication and provide more uniform lubrication to each section. 1. For example, when swabbing sections 1-5 of a 10-section machine, the first swab cycle would start on section #1 (1, 2, 3, 4, 5), the next swab cycle would start with section #2 (2, 3, 4, 5, 1), etc. 2. When swabbing sections 6-10, the first swab cycle would start on section #6 (6, 7, 8, 9, 10), the next swab cycle would start with section #7 (7, 8, 9, 10, 6), etc.

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Swab NNPB blanks only from the baffle parting line down to the load line, which is the top portion of the blank. 1. Use either a patting motion or one downward sweeping motion. 2. Do not swab blanks with an upward motion. 1. Swab B&B blanks from the load line down to the neckring parting line, which is the bottom portion of the blank. 1. Use a downward motion of the swab. 2. Do not swab with an upward motion, double-pump the swab, or use a scrubbing motion. 1. Swab B&B blanks with post-style baffles and valve baffles from the baffle-match down to the neckring parting line, which includes the entire blank cavity. 1. Always use a downward motion. 2. Do not swab with an upward motion, double-pump the swab, or use a scrubbing motion. 1. Swab “41” process blanks from the bottom using an upward motion. 1. Make one motion, passing the swab up the cavity of the blank. Do not use a scrubbing action.

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 2. Sometimes it may be necessary to lightly swab the baffle end of the blank, either by itself or with the blank cavity. 1. To swab the baffles, perform the following steps: Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Only swab baffles as necessary, and after the blanks have been swabbed for the section. 1. Using the blank swab brush, swab the baffles with a patting motion. Punted baffles may require a special circular swab technique to swab the entire baffle. 1. Do not scrape or drag the swab over the baffles because it will leave a buildup of lubricant. 1. Work from the inside baffle outward toward yourself. 1. If possible, rotate the swab brush after swabbing each section, and shake it slightly to ensure that a uniform amount of lubricant is applied to each baffle. 1. To swab the mould side forming equipment, perform the following steps: Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. When swabbing both the blank side and mould side of the forming machine at the same time, use the swab cycle button. 1. Unless otherwise programmed, for an O-I forming machine, push in the Mould Side Inhibit

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) safety switch to disable all functions that are listed in Run Mould Side Inhibit on the INI file. 1. Do not put your thumb or finger through the ring on the swab brush handle, if your plant uses swabs with a ring. NOTE: Serious injuries to your thumb or fingers may result if the swab gets caught in the section. Do not place thumb or fingers in the ring! 1. For mould side swabs, cut the ring off, if it exists, and add an extension as needed. 1. Wait until the moulds are fully open and the takeout arm has stopped over the deadplate before swabbing. 1. Using one blank swab brush, start swabbing from the inside cavity to the outside cavity, working toward yourself. 1. Swab the top of the moulds with a very dry swab according to the job history. 1. Place the swab on top of the inside mould (right or left side) and pat it lightly outward across the top of the moulds. 2. Repeat on the other side. 3. Avoid swabbing over the cooling holes on the top of the moulds so they don’t become blocked

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) with swabbing compound 4. Rotate the swab and shake it slightly between each application to prevent uneven application of the lubricant and irregular swab wear. 1. Swab the mould shoulders and body decorations with a very dry swab per the swabbing instructions if necessary and according to the job history. 1. Use an upward motion to swab the inside cavity of each mould shoulder. 2. Swab all the mould cavities on one side (right or left), then the other side. 1. Rotate the swab and shake it slightly between each application to prevent uneven application of the lubricant and irregular swab wear. 1. Swab bottom plates with a semi-dry swab if necessary and according to the job history. 1. Place the swab on the inside bottom plate, and lightly drag it outward across the bottom plates using a sliding motion. 1. Upon completion of tasks, perform the following steps: Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Perform basic housekeeping duties. Clean up the work space, tools and equipment, dispose of trash, put tools and equipment in assigned area. 1. Record and report findings and results.

Step Instruction Images Images & Comments (Plant Specific) 1. Follow appropriate instructions for notification of findings and results relating to specifications, targets and/or reaction limits. 1. Required Training: Required Training Documents Before performing this work instruction, applicable personnel must be trained by a qualified trainer on the required training contents listed. Swabbing Techniques – annual training renewal mandatory in Asia Pacific and Europe 1. Equipment: Mandatory Equipment Acceptable Models or Requirements Model Used (Plant Specific) Swab brushes – various sizes Commercial swab lubricant compound for blanks Commercial swab lubricant compound for neckrings Light oil Optional or Recommended Equipment Acceptable Models or Requirements Model Used (Plant Specific) 1. Definitions:

Term Definition Swabbing Process of applying lubricant to improve release of the glass ware from the blank and mould parts. 1. References: External documents that were used in the development of this document 1. Appendix Information referenced in previous sections. 1.
